page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs with 24 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 93.0 GB of system memory, which equates to approximately 3.88 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU from the Turing architecture family, which includes 16 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and relies on network-attached storage, operating with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics. Single-core CPU performance is relatively low, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though the PassMark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%. Notably, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong results in LLM inference tasks. Prompt processing for both 135M and 7B models reaches top-tier performance in the top 10%, while text generation for a 7B model is rated as strong.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of high-end tensor-core accelerators. The lack of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which should be factored into architectural planning. This server is well-suited for workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, ray tracing, and parallelized compute tasks that can leverage GPU acceleration, while it is less optimal for single-threaded CPU-bound applications.
